Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, the two main forms of IBD, are typically treated only after symptoms appear, when the gut has already been damaged. items.summary: “합격하고 싶은 간절함이 기도로만 끝나면, 그건 간절한 게 아니지요.” 해마다 11월 중순경 치러지는 대학수학능력시험(수능)을 앞두고 이미 전국 사찰에선 ‘수능 백일 기도회’ 등이 한창이다. 경북 경산 팔공산 갓바위 선본사, 서울 강북구 도선사, 경남 남해 금산 보리암 등 입소문이 난 곳은 매일매일 인산인해다. 대한불교조계종 도선사 주지인 도심 스님은 10일 동아일보와 만나 “수능 기도는 공부도 안 했는데 붙여 달라고 비는 게 아니다”라고 했다. ―도선사에서도 수능 백일 기도회가 열리고 있습니다. “매년 수능일을 앞두고 대웅전 옆 석불전(石佛殿) 앞에서 열고 있습니다. 석불전은 암벽을 깎아 만든 마애불(磨崖佛)인데, 신라 말기 도선국사가 절을 창건하면서 만들었다고 해요. 세월이 흐르면서 전각은 다시 짓고 바뀌었지만, 마애불은 그대로라 가장 영험한 곳으로 알려진 거죠. 그래서 조선 시대에도 과거 시험을 보는 선비들과 가족들이 많이 찾았어요. 그게 지금까지 이어진 것 같습니다.”

items.title: The Guardian view on plague in Russia: what is most worrying is the lack of information | Editorial
items.summary: In the three weeks since a health worker’s death in Siberia, officials have stonewalled the WHO – setting a worrying precedent for future pandemics Is there a plague outbreak in Russia? If the answer were a clear yes, there shouldn’t be much reason to worry. With swift medical intervention, plague is treatable. But in the nearly three weeks since a worker at a Siberian plague research unit died of a mysterious respiratory illness, state officials have been consistently tight-lipped about what happened and whether there were any further cases. It is this uncertainty that has the World Health Organization (WHO) and international community worried: partly because there is a – very small – risk of an outbreak, and partly because it is yet another warning that the international coordination we rely on to prevent pandemics is fraying along with the rest of international politics, and could easily fail to protect us in the future. items.title: Hiding in plane sight: the invisible turbulence that can strike out of a clear blue sky
items.summary: As the planet warms, airlines are grappling with what this means for air travel – and for the passengers who simply refuse to keep their seatbelts fastened It was a swelteringly hot afternoon in south-west Myanmar on 21 May 2024. Tropical thunderstorms, showers and highs of 36C were forecast for the area around the Irrawaddy Basin. High above, monsoonal heat and humidity were building into a vast convective column of water vapour, a towering cumulonimbus cloud soaring up to 35,000ft (more than 10,500 metres) into the air. From the ground, it would have looked like something from a children’s picture book – a soft, fluffy white mass. But for Singapore Airlines flight SQ321 passing just above, it was anything but benign. In the cabin of the Boeing 777, passengers were being woken up for breakfast with three hours to go on the journey from London to Singapore. For the 210 travellers on board, the past 10 hours had been uneventful. The seatbelt signs were off. Some were milling around, others were using the toilets, and cabin staff were preparing trolleys for service. At 2.19pm and 23 seconds local time, moderate turbulence shook the plane for 17 seconds and the seatbelt sign was switched on. Then, as one passenger described it, it was “like a grenade had gone off”. In just 4.6 seconds, any passenger not strapped in hit the roof with 1.5 times the force of gravity and was thrown back on the floor in an instant. Continue reading...

articles.title: “간절함이 기도로만 끝난다면 그건 정말 간절한게 아닙니다”
articles.snippet: “합격하고 싶은 간절함이 기도로만 끝나면, 그건 간절한 게 아니지요.” 해마다 11월 중순경 치러지는 대학수학능력시험(수능)을 앞두고 이미 전국 사찰에선 ‘수능 백일 기도회’ 등이 한창이다. 경북 경산 팔공산 갓바위 선본사, 서울 강북구 도선사, 경남 남해 금산 보리암 등 입소문이 난 곳은 매일매일 인산인해다. 대한불교조계종 도선사 주지인 도심 스님은 10일 동아일보와 만나 “수능 기도는 공부도 안 했는데 붙여 달라고 비는 게 아니다”라고 했다. ―도선사에서도 수능 백일 기도회가 열리고 있습니다. “매년 수능일을 앞두고 대웅전 옆 석불전(石佛殿) 앞에서 열고 있습니다. 석불전은 암벽을 깎아 만든 마애불(磨崖佛)인데, 신라 말기 도선국사가 절을 창건하면서 만들었다고 해요. 세월이 흐르면서 전각은 다시 짓고 바뀌었지만, 마애불은 그대로라 가장 영험한 곳으로 알려진 거죠. 그래서 조선 시대에도 과거 시험을 보는 선비들과 가족들이 많이 찾았어요. 그게 지금까지 이어진 것 같습니다.”

articles.title: “보고싶은 아빠, 꼭 다시 만나요” 순직 소방관 7세 딸의 편지
articles.snippet: “아빠, 나중에 꼭 다시 만나요. 그때는 제가 어른이 됐을 때일 거예요.” 18일 경기 부천시 순천향대 부천병원에 마련된 고 김진석 소방위(44)의 빈소. 영정 사진 앞에는 그의 7세 외동딸이 직접 쓴 손편지가 놓여 있었다. 김 양은 편지에 “아빠 어제 돌아가셨는데 지금도 너무 보고 싶네요. 우린 지금 장례식장이에요”라며 “전 알아요 아빠는 저를 제일 사랑하셨다는 거”라고 썼다. 이어 “사랑해요, 보고 싶은 아빠”라며 세상을 떠난 아빠를 그리워했다. 편지 한편에는 출동하는 소방차 모습도 그려 넣었다. 삐뚤빼뚤한 글씨로 아빠를 향한 그리움을 담아낸 편지에 빈소를 찾은 조문객들은 눈물을 참지 못했다. 동료 소방관들도 “왜 우리 진석이한테 이런 일이…”라며 말을 잇지 못했다. ● 퇴근 20분 전 ‘마지막 출동’에 귀환 못해 부천소방서 오정119안전센터 소속인 김 소방위는 16일 오전 8시 38분경 경기 부천시의 한 도장 공장에서 불이 났다는 신고를 받고 소방차에 몸을 실었다.

articles.title: The Guardian view on Stormont: voters in Northern Ireland deserve more than an endless cycle of dysfunction | Editorial
articles.snippet: After the executive’s failure to set a budget, and renewed culture-war confrontations, faith in the government’s ability to act in the common good is evaporating Late last month, protesters deposited a sizable amount of foul-smelling green water on the steps of Stormont to draw attention to the appalling state of Lough Neagh, the largest freshwater lake in the British Isles. Years of agricultural pollution have created an environmental disaster in an area of huge ecological significance that once inspired the poetry of Seamus Heaney. Its plight should be a top priority for Northern Ireland’s devolved government. But the executive currently has other matters on its mind. The sentencing of the former leader of the Democratic Unionist party (DUP) Jeffrey Donaldson, after he was convicted of child sexual abuse, dominated Thursday’s headlines. Meanwhile, a cross-party political crisis continues to play out. Halfway through the financial year, Stormont has yet to set a budget. The current deadlock in negotiations with the Northern Ireland secretary, Sir Chris Bryant, could lead to one being imposed from Westminster. articles.title: ‘Stranger than stranger-than-fiction’: how Lance Oppenheim made the year’s two buzziest films
articles.snippet: Primetime and You Can See Everything are both clammy, audacious awards contenders that challenge our sense of reality. Ahead of the release of his drama starring Robert Pattinson as a TV vigilante, the 30-year-old director talks crime, punishment and South Park To direct one movie that is on everyone’s lips in awards season is remarkable. To make two begins to look like sorcery. That is the position in which the 30-year-old Florida-born film-maker Lance Oppenheim now finds himself. Next month brings the release of You Can See Everything, the three-hour documentary which he co-directed with faux-naif deadpan imp Nathan Fielder, in which they spend a month living with the disgraced health-tech mogul Elizabeth Holmes before she begins her 11-year prison sentence for fraud and conspiracy. The film, described by Oppenheim as “head-spinning” and so shrouded in secrecy that Variety magazine’s list of Oscar predictions identifies one of its cast members only as “[Redacted]”, is expected to become the first documentary nominated for best picture. When I meet Oppenheim in a London hotel, it is to discuss his other hot ticket, Primetime, for which Robert Pattinson is the one attracting Oscar buzz. The Batman actor gives a high-wire performance as Chris Hansen, the sensationalist US television vigilante renowned for ambushing paedophiles on To Catch a Predator, which was a disreputable and highly addictive segment of the current affairs show Dateline NBC between 2004 and 2007. Hansen later parlayed the idea, and his crusading shtick, into a succession of spin-offs. Some, including Hansen Vs Predators, had the same sleazy catnip quality. Others, such as a sting to collar bicycle thieves, did not. Continue reading...

articles.title: An open book: how to make a great film adaptation, from The Shining to Trainspotting
articles.snippet: Not every great novel makes a great movie, and sometimes the opposite is true. But regardless of the source text, or how beloved characters are treated, there is more than one way to write a successful adaptation It is always fun to join in a craze, like a Victorian going mad for penny farthings. Which is probably why, against my better judgment, I went to see Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster The Odyssey this summer, buying my ticket into the popular conversation along with everyone else. This year’s other divisive adaptation, Emerald Fennell’s Wuthering Heights, had the world and his wife arguing about it before they had even watched the film. No doubt the makers of the recent Sense and Sensibility movie were also hoping for lots of people to go and see it to discover whether they hated it. After all, very few of us leave the cinema saying: “That’s exactly how I pictured it in my head.” Or even less likely: “That was better than the book.” We’re more likely to shake our fists at how they ruined the ending, dumbed it down, unforgivably cast somebody with the wrong hair, or betrayed a beloved character, as with last year’s Thursday Murder Club debacle. articles.title: The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable review – Netflix doc on ‘secret album’ is strictly for super fans
articles.snippet: The lore of Once Upon a Time in Shaolin, once bought by Martin Shkreli, is explored in a rambling film produced by RZA For every reason except one, Once Upon a Time in Shaolin, the seventh album by the Wu-Tang Clan, should’ve been a commercial hit. The 31-track double album, recorded in secret between 2007 and 2013, reunited all of the remaining members of the hallowed Staten Island rap crew and featured eye-catching collaborators from the standard (Redman, offshoot group Wu-Tang Killa Bees) to the unexpected (Cher, Game of Thrones actor Carice van Houten). The sound, at least according to those involved, harkened back to the glory days of the group’s beginnings in the 90s. But for years, almost no one heard it. The group only issued a single copy of Once Upon a Time in Shaolin – on CD, ensconced within layers of filigreed silver – with the stipulation, in legalese, that it could not be used for any commercial purposes for 88 years. The decree, either a stunt or a bold artistic statement on streaming’s devaluation of music, depending on your generosity and perhaps your net worth, succeeded in drumming up plenty of hype. And if you were anywhere around the blogosphere or cable news in 2015, you may recall that the beneficiary of that hype – the purchaser and thus single intended listener of this $2m musical treasure – was one Martin Shkreli, the “pharma bro” widely despised for gleefully hiking the costs of prescription drugs for profit.
